decision.summary: Dispatch consumes the live provider report, but ordinary priority preemption does not. The incumbent can be terminated for an urgent task that the same tick refuses to dispatch.

accepted_areas.evidence: task_execution_dispatch_candidate is consumed by dispatch_ready_tasks and higher_priority_ready_task_exists for review, finalize, in-progress, todo, ownership, reviewer, and dependency decisions.
The preemption loop applies unchanged-event cooldown, failure-loop exclusion, and chair-reassignment triage before selecting a candidate.
Active and queued work for the logical agent are counted; preemption occurs only when an unserved urgent candidate exceeds free logical slots.

The 300-second default gates only higher_priority_ready_task_exists. Assignment changes, chair completion, dead-worker completion, and other legitimate cleanup remain outside this ordinary-priority gate.

blocking_findings.dispatch_behavior: agent_auto_dispatch_block_reason(config, state, agent_id, provider_report) rejects local_cli_worker_supported=false.
blocking_findings.preemption_behavior: higher_priority_ready_task_exists has no provider_report input; agent_can_take_task does not reject local_cli_worker_supported=false or supports_auto_approve=false, so it returns a preemption decision of true.
blocking_findings.impact: The supervisor can SIGTERM a healthy incumbent for an urgent candidate and then fail to launch the replacement, recreating worker churn under a provider-readiness failure.
blocking_findings.required_correction: Use one in-cycle provider-readiness decision for dispatch and preemption, account for the slot that incumbent termination would release, and add local-CLI plus adapter auto-delivery regressions.
